title: Binary tree
short: Nodes that branch into at most two children.
what: A binary tree starts at one node, the root. Each node has at most two children, left and right, and a node with no children is a leaf. Most tree answers come from asking the children first and combining what they say.
analogy: A family tree drawn upside down, where every parent has at most two kids.

frames.say: 3 is the root. It has two children, 9 and 20. 9, 15 and 7 have no children: they are leaves.
How deep is the tree? A node's depth is 1 + the deeper of its two subtrees. So the root asks its children first.
9 is a leaf. Its missing children count as 0, so 9 answers 1 + 0 = 1.
20 asks its own children. 15 and 7 are leaves, so each answers 1.
20 answers 1 + max(1, 1) = 2 back up to the root.
The root answers 1 + max(1, 2) = 3. Each node was visited once, so the work is O(n).

when: The input is a TreeNode root
Depth, height, diameter or path sum
Visit the tree level by level
A node's answer depends on its children's answers
watch: Handle the None child first. It is the base case that stops the recursion.
A binary tree is not sorted by itself. A sorted one is a binary search tree.
A very lopsided tree is as deep as a linked list, and deep recursion can hit Python's limit of about 1000 calls.
